# International Break {.unnumbered}

Using this break to investigate a thought, or worry, that occurred to me - is it generally a riskier idea to pick players from the same team? Will it make my points more volatile, based on the idea that scores for players in the same team might be more positively correlated?

## Correlations

### All correlations
First, let's get every player's points time series up to GW10, and get every single correlation of each player, with every other player.
```{python}
#| echo: false
from fpl.correlation import plot_all_correlations, plot_multiple_correlations 

gw=10

plot_all_correlations(gw)['plot']
```

Looks roughly normal with a bit of positive skew.

### Intra-team correlations
```{python}
#| echo: false
from fpl.correlation import plot_all_correlations, plot_multiple_correlations 

gw=10

plot_all_correlations(gw=gw, same_team=1)['plot']
```

Already this looks like there's more of a bulge of mass on the positive side. This seems to support the hypothesis, but hard to say if this is significant without some kind of direct comparison.

### Intra-position correlations
```{python}
#| echo: false
from fpl.correlation import plot_all_correlations, plot_multiple_correlations 

gw=10

plot_all_correlations(gw=gw, same_position=1)['plot']
```

This just looks very similar to the "All correlations" histogram. I think that's to be expected - why would we expect that e.g. midfielders all score particular similarly or particularly differently across different teams.

### Intra-team-position correlations
```{python}
#| echo: false
from fpl.correlation import plot_all_correlations, plot_multiple_correlations 

gw=10

plot_all_correlations(gw=gw, same_team=1, same_position=1)['plot']
```

Looks similar to the intra-team picture. Would we expect players in the same team and the same position to have correlated scores? Perhaps it depends on the position - defenders all get a clean sheet together, but only the scoring player gets the points (and is less likely to be a defender)

## Comparing correlations
It's hard to compare whether correlations are different between the groups, so we'll conduct some comparisons. We'll normalise the histograms to account the different volumes, so that we're only comparing their shapes.

### Inter-team vs Intra-team
```{python}
#| echo: false
from fpl.correlation import plot_all_correlations, plot_multiple_correlations 

gw=10

plot_multiple_correlations(same_team_1=1, label_1 = 'Intra-team correlations',
different_team_2=1, label_2 = 'Inter-team correlations')
```

The blue peeking out on the right shows that players' scores tend to be slightly more correlated with their teammates', compared with players in other teams.

### Inter-position vs Intra-position
```{python}
#| echo: false
from fpl.correlation import plot_all_correlations, plot_multiple_correlations 

gw=10

plot_multiple_correlations(same_position_1=1, label_1 = 'Intra-position correlations',
different_position_2=1, label_2 = 'Inter-position correlations')
```

Looks very insignificant.

### Inter-position-team vs all correlations
```{python}
#| echo: false
from fpl.correlation import plot_all_correlations, plot_multiple_correlations 

gw=10

plot_multiple_correlations(label_1 = 'All correlations',
same_position_2=1, same_team_2=1, label_2 = 'Intra-position-team correlations')
```

This is interesting - the intra-position-team position is flatter and wider. This supports the clean-sheet X scorers observation that some correlations are very positive (clean sheets) and some are very negative (scorers). Let's look at it more closely:

### Intra-team correlations per position

### Goalkeeper
```{python}
#| echo: false
from fpl.correlation import plot_all_correlations, plot_multiple_correlations 

gw=10

plot_multiple_correlations(label_1 = 'All correlations',
same_position_2=1, same_team_2=1, label_2 = 'Intra-position-team correlations',
force_position = 1)
```

This makes a lot of sense. Generally, between goalkeepers on the same team, only one of them will play so one will score at least 2, and the other will score probably nothing. So a negative correlation makes complete sense. This discussion is fairly redundant except as a sense check given you can only play one GK. Although perhaps it suggests that the safest way to ensure your GK scores at least 2 points is to have two GKs from the same team? Even this is a bit redundant because between two starting keepers, it seems unlikely that they both don't play, so the additional likelihood is probably not worth the points differential between the sub keeper and the starting keeper from another team.

### Defender
```{python}
#| echo: false
from fpl.correlation import plot_all_correlations, plot_multiple_correlations 

gw=10

plot_multiple_correlations(label_1 = 'All correlations',
same_position_2=1, same_team_2=1, label_2 = 'Intra-position-team correlations',
force_position = 2)
```

Defenders' scores tend to be more positively correlated. Again, makes sense because all defenders receive or don't receive the clean sheet together.

### Midfielder
```{python}
#| echo: false
from fpl.correlation import plot_all_correlations, plot_multiple_correlations 

gw=10

plot_multiple_correlations(label_1 = 'All correlations',
same_position_2=1, same_team_2=1, label_2 = 'Intra-position-team correlations',
force_position = 3)
```

Probably nothing too significant here - a slight bias towards more negative correlation

### Forward
```{python}
#| echo: false
from fpl.correlation import plot_all_correlations, plot_multiple_correlations 

gw=10

plot_multiple_correlations(label_1 = 'All correlations',
same_position_2=1, same_team_2=1, label_2 = 'Intra-position-team correlations',
force_position = 4)
```

A bit more of a bias towards negative skew here. Probably because goals are worth a lot of points and the most someone else gets is the assist.

## Conclusion
So what do I take from this?

### Intra-team correlations are not categorically risky
I'm not concerned that the notion of having 3 players from one team is inherently risky. But:

### Intra-team-position correlations can be risky or useful

Having multiple players from the same team and the same position can be a risk or an opportunity. Looking at the flatter Intra-position-team comparison graph, I need to choose pairs/triples that are negatively correlated, to minimise volatility. Based on what we see:

- Goalkeepers from the same team tend to have negative correlated scores, but given that it seems very unlikely for two starting GKs from different teams to both not play, it's probably not worth the cost of lower points expectations (from the sub keeper) in return a potentially lower volatility

- Defenders on the same team have signficantly more positively correlated scores (compared with all correlations). I should be careful before selecting defenders from the same team - their sum is more likely to score very high or very low, whereas I would much rather something in the middle more reliably.

- Midfielder intra-team-position correlations don't bear much thought - their distribution is very similar to the all correlations distribution

- (Good) Forwards from the same team is a good idea (compared with forwards from separate teams) because they tend to be more negatively correlated.
